question.text: Zenith Private Equity AIF (Cat II) is about to appoint a custodian. The sponsor group owns 30% of Prism Custody Services Ltd. Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, can Prism Custody Services be appointed as custodian?

answer.text: Yes — related-party custodians are permitted without any conditions for Cat I/II AIFs
Yes — related-party appointment is allowed only if the corpus is below INR 500 crore
No — custodian must always be a public-sector entity like SHCIL
No — the custodian shall not be a related party to the sponsors or designated partners UNLESS specific conditions prescribed under the regulations are fulfilled

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the custodian of an AIF shall not be a related party to the sponsors or designated partners unless specific conditions prescribed under the regulations are fulfilled. A 30% sponsor-group holding in Prism makes it a related party, so appointment is permitted only if the prescribed conditions are satisfied. The Trap: The unconditional-permission option ignores the related-party bar. The INR 500 crore corpus option invents a threshold not in the source. The public-sector-only option fabricates a rule; the regulations do not restrict custodians to public-sector entities. Note: When relying on the related-party carve-out, confirm that each of the specific conditions in the regulations is met before appointment.
